meta.title: Pelican Packaging: reserve, build or bridge?
meta.subtitle: Recommendation on the second molding-line installation slot, the full line order and temporary overflow capacity · Investment Committee pre-read for decision at the January 2027 IC
meta.purpose: Decide whether to reserve a second molding-line installation slot now, build immediately, or buy temporary overflow capacity
meta.confidentiality: Synthetic benchmark data · built only from the IC briefing pack; no external research · cash figures exclude 2027–30 operating cash flow, which the pack does not give

inputs.label: Finished analysis deck, extracted to text

storyline.governing_thought: Reserve the slot as a capped $0.6M option, bridge 2028 with the contract molder, and order the line only once signed demand and funding clear set triggers

exec_summary.text: The gap is real and starts in 2028, but its size hinges on unsigned demand

sub_points.text: On accepted units the line is 92% used in 2027, not 83%; overflow starts in 2028 (0.6M)
Overflow hits 3.5M units by 2030 at forecast, 0.9M at signed minimums; 2.6M is unsigned
The 98% fill rate is monthly; two misses let a customer rebid its whole allocation

exec_summary.text: Ordering now breaks the cash covenant; doing nothing breaks the fill-rate standard

sub_points.text: A full order leaves $4.0M of cash, $3.0M under the $7.0M floor, with no facility
Doing nothing leaves 0.6M units unserved in 2028, 3.5M by 2030; the molder is 1.0M short in 2030

exec_summary.text: The slot is a capped option worth buying, provided the order date can move

sub_points.text: Cash stays $1.2M above the floor, at most $0.6M is lost, and it pays only by protecting allocations
It expects a June 2027 order, but funding is only plausible in 2028: agree a later date first

exec_summary.text: Three hard triggers turn the reservation into a full order

sub_points.text: Demand: 10.5M+ units signed for 2029 or 2030 (now 9.4M / 9.8M), or a simulated 2-month breach
Funding: $3.5M+ committed, so cash after the $4.2M payment stays at $7.5M or more
Readiness: supplier dates and validation plan confirmed; decide Q1 2028, Q3 at the latest

next_steps.action: Supplier terms (order date, lead time, price)

lead_message.text: Reserving now and gating the order survives our tests, but only with a funding plan and a flexible order date

bullets: **Wrong denominator:** it divides units started by nameplate hours and reports quality rejects separately, so it overstates headroom
**2027 slack:** really 0.7M units (7.8%), not the 1.7M (17%) the KPI implies
**Specialty scrap:** 4% more scrap than the standard mix, with no allowance in the forecast, costs about 0.09–0.10M units of capacity a year from 2029

Ops KPI = units started ÷ 10.0M nameplate hours; quality rejects are subtracted only in a separate report

lead_message.text: The gap hinges on unsigned demand: overflow reaches 3.5M units by 2030 at forecast, but only 0.9M at signed minimums

slides.rationale: Three demand cases over four years against one ceiling -> clustered columns with a benchmark line
slides.unit_line: **Overflow above internal capacity**, millions of accepted units, 2027–30; dashed line = molder ceiling of 2.5M

bullets: **Unsigned volume:** 2.6M (21%) of the 12.4M units forecast for 2030 sit above signed minimums and are nonbinding
**Timing:** two key design programs slipped a quarter last year; a one-year slip pushes the molder ceiling breach from 2030 to 2031
**Mix:** specialty volume adds roughly 0.1M units of overflow a year through extra scrap
sidebar.implication: Only the forecast case needs a second line before 2031; committing $4.8M before customers sign is a bet on that case, so signed volume should trigger the order

basis.header: How the 2030 forecast overflow is built

footnotes: Overflow = demand above 9.0M practical capacity plus the specialty scrap allowance (20% of 2029–30 units × 4%); no specialty volume assumed in 2028
Slip case = forecast delayed one year; 2030 specialty share of 20% — both analysis assumptions

lead_message.text: Annual totals understate the risk: fill rate is monthly, and with the molder maxed out 2029 uses 98% of monthly supply

slides.rationale: Monthly demand against maximum supply by year -> data table (as in the source)
slides.unit_line: **Average month at forecast demand**, millions of accepted units, 2028–30

sidebar.header: One bad month can cost an allocation
bullets: **Standard:** a 98% fill rate every month for every customer; two misses give the right to rebid the whole allocation, not just the units missed
**Peaks:** several launches in one six-week window can exceed the monthly rate even when the year fits (plant supervisor); molder holiday capacity is uncommitted
**At stake:** about $4.0M a year of base contribution (9.0M units × $0.45) is exposed; losing a quarter of it costs ~$1.0M a year, more than the $0.45M lost on the 2030 shortfall
**To confirm:** a monthly simulation or an inventory buffer

rows.label: Max supply: internal after scrap + molder (2.5M ÷ 12)
Demand as % of max monthly supply
How far a peak month can exceed the average

slides.so_what: In 2029 even the molder leaves ~2% headroom: a launch cluster could cause the two misses that open a rebid
footnotes: Monthly rates = annual capacity ÷ 12 (even-flow simplification)
Contribution proxy uses the pack's $0.45 a unit for serving rather than refusing demand; the 25% loss share is an illustrative analysis assumption

lead_message.text: Ordering now would leave $4.0M of cash, $3.0M under the floor, and the growth claim behind it shows no causation

lead_message.text: Only 'reserve the slot + molder bridge' passes every hard constraint while keeping 2030 capacity available

slides.rationale: Four paths on the same criteria -> comparison table
slides.unit_line: **Four paths against the hard constraints**; forecast overflow 0.6M units in 2028 and 3.5M in 2030; costs are 2027–30 incremental cash

cells.text: Covered if triggers met by Q3 2028

callout.detail: No capacity lost against ordering now; no covenant breach, no $4.8M bet on unsigned demand

footnotes: Source: IC briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis
Recommended $5.8M = $4.8M line (deposit credited, not double-counted) + $0.07M 2028 premium + $0.14M H1 2029 premium + $0.83M fixed cost, mid-2029 to 2030
The recommended path costs $0.6M less than ordering now ($6.45M) because line fixed costs start about 18 months later
Costs: capex, $0.55M a year fixed from commissioning, $0.12 premium and $0.45 lost contribution per unit; excl. operating cash flow and post-2030 value

lead_message.text: The molder is a cheap bridge through 2029, but at forecast runs out in 2030 and cannot make specialty containers

slides.rationale: Volume against the ceiling, and what it costs -> two panels over the same years
slides.unit_line: **Contract molder as the overflow bridge**, at forecast demand, 2028–30

bullets: **2028–29:** overflow uses 24%, then 92% of the ceiling, leaving 0.2M units of slack in 2029
**2030:** overflow is 140% of the ceiling; 1.0M units go unserved
**Specialty:** 20% of 2029 units (2.24M) is not validated at the molder, so it runs in-house and takes the internal slack; notice is five months, holiday capacity uncommitted
**Still worth using:** the molder keeps $0.33 of the $0.45 unit contribution, against $0 for a refused order

panels.unit_line: **Forecast overflow incl. specialty scrap**, M units; dashed = ceiling

panels.header: Premiums stay small; 2030 adds lost contribution

slides.so_what: Use the molder for 2028–29; it cannot replace the line if forecast 2030 demand arrives
footnotes: Units sent to the molder: 0.6M (2028), 2.29M (2029), 2.5M cap (2030). Premium of $0.12 per accepted unit excludes first-article validation for the specialty product

lead_message.text: The line insures allocations rather than margin and beats the molder on running cost only above 4.6M units a year

slides.rationale: What separates the two paths' 2030 economics -> bridge from molder-only to new line
slides.unit_line: **2030 net contribution on overflow at forecast, before the $4.8M capex**, $ millions a year

sidebar.caption: M overflow units a year = $0.55M fixed cost ÷ $0.12 premium
bullets: **Inside the 2.5M ceiling:** buying beats building, even before capex; overflow peaks at 3.5M
**Protects:** peak fill rate (~$4.0M a year at stake), specialty, post-2030 growth
sidebar.implication: Because the case rests on protecting allocations, the order trigger should be signed customer volume, not forecast margin

footnotes: The line earns only ~$0.20M a year more than the molder in 2030 but leaves no units unserved; the molder leaves 1.0M unserved (a rebid trigger)
Each 1M units of growth after 2030 above the molder ceiling adds $0.45M a year to the line's advantage
No salvage value, useful life or discount rate is given, so the comparison is on annual running economics only; $0.45 and $0.12 are not compared as if they were alternative price quotes

lead_message.text: The slot risks at most $0.6M and keeps cash above the floor, but pays off only by averting a rebid

slides.rationale: Break-even probabilities under three loss cases -> grid kept as a table
slides.unit_line: **Loss avoided if 2030 capacity is late by one year**, and the chance the slot must avert it to repay the $0.6M deposit

sidebar.caption: the most the slot can lose: credited if the line is ordered, forfeited if not
bullets: **Cash:** $8.2M left, $1.2M above the floor; the deposit uses a third of the $1.8M headroom; the $4.2M balance needs $3.0M+ new money
**Odds:** pays at a ~1-in-4 to 2-in-5 chance of keeping an allocation; plausible, but only if it buys timing (H6)

slides.so_what: Pay the deposit as insurance only if its order date can be deferred, or it lapses before funding
footnotes: Break-even probability = $0.6M at risk ÷ loss avoided. Rebid shares are illustrative analysis assumptions (not verified), on the 9.0M-unit base × $0.45
Scale check, signed-minimum case: $0.6M equals ~5.5 years of the 2030 molder premium ($0.11M); headroom left covers $0.35M of 2028–29 premiums

lead_message.text: Reserving the slot becomes a bad option under five conditions; the two most likely can be tested before the March deposit

slides.rationale: Five conditions, each with harm, test and timing -> table (as in the source)
slides.unit_line: **Conditions that destroy the slot's value**, with the test or mitigation for each

rows.label: 1 · Order due by June 2027, funding plausible only in 2028

cells.text: Negotiate an order date of Q1 2028 or later (install H1 2029); otherwise decline

rows.label: 2 · Slot buys nothing scarce: 12-month lead time available anyway

cells.text: $0.6M paid for timing we would get anyway
Get written lead time and crew availability without a slot
Overflow of 0.9M or less; molder covers it for $0.11M a year or less
Track signed volume quarterly; kill at the go/no-go gate
Line arrives a year early with $0.55M a year of fixed cost
Use the deferral right; molder covers 2030 at 92% of its ceiling
Deposit uses $0.6M of $1.8M headroom; pre-build and validation compete for the rest
13-week cash forecast; cap pre-build working capital

slides.so_what: No later order date: decline, use the molder, order in 2028 at standard lead time
footnotes: Source: IC briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis
If the supplier will not move the order date to Q1 2028 or later, decline the slot and plan on the molder plus a 2028 order at standard lead time, once confirmed
The pack gives no slot expiry or deferral terms; the June 2027 date comes from its 'if ordered by June 2027, machine expected mid-2028'

lead_message.text: Cover 2028 in three layers: the contract molder booked by June 2027, a 2027 safety stock, and specialty kept in-house

slides.rationale: Three parallel layers of cover -> text columns, each with its number

columns.header: A. External capacity: book the contract molder
detail: Needed: only a January 2027 order, which breaches the covenant, beats the 2028 peak
Notice is 5 months; sign by end-June 2027 to lock in holiday capacity
Hold an option on up to 2.3M units for 2029 (~$0.27M)
Quote specialty first-article validation as a hedge

columns.header: B. Internal buffer: build a 2027 safety stock
detail: Slack of 9.0M − 8.3M exceeds the 0.6M 2028 overflow
Pre-build standard containers ahead of the 2028 peak to absorb launch clustering
Depends on shelf-life and customer lot rules
Cap working capital so cash headroom holds (unit cost not in pack)

columns.header: C. Internal mix: protect what only we can make
columns.point_caption: M units a year of scrap allowance
detail: Schedule specialty first on our own line; the molder is not validated for it
Add the 4% specialty scrap allowance to the plan
Run a monthly fill-rate simulation (launches, holidays, scrap) by Q2 2027

slides.so_what: Together: up to 3.2M units of 2028 cover, ~5 times the overflow, with no fixed capex
footnotes: The pack says the 2028 peak starts before mid-2028; the analysis assumes around Q2 2028, so the latest molder notice is about November 2027

lead_message.text: Release the $4.2M balance only when all three triggers are met on demand, funding and readiness

slides.rationale: Three conditions that must all hold -> pillars

body.foundation: Not triggers: 'demand is growing', nonbinding forecasts, peer growth statistics, or a wish to announce capacity publicly

items.header: Demand: signed 2029 or 2030 minimums of 10.5M units or more
detail: Counts take-or-pay or prepaid volume
OR: simulation shows 2+ months below 98% with the molder at contracted capacity
Why 10.5M: signed overflow (~1.6M) uses two-thirds of the ceiling; under half of the other 1.9M forecast units would exhaust it

items.header: Funding: at least $3.5M committed, so cash after the payment is $7.5M or more
items.point_caption: balance due after the credited deposit
detail: $8.2M − $4.2M + $3.5M = $7.5M: the $7.0M floor plus a $0.5M buffer
Customer prepayment, or a loan backed by a signed-volume guarantee; pricing to negotiate
One signed-volume guarantee can meet two triggers: it adds demand and secures the loan

items.header: Readiness: supplier and validation plan confirmed
items.point_caption: months to install, fixed price, confirmed
detail: Plan allows +2 months for specialty validation
Molder bridge contracted through commissioning
Construction inflation re-quoted

footnotes: The 10.5M threshold and the $0.5M buffer are the analysis's proposals (policy choices, not in the pack; unverified)
Internal capacity after specialty scrap ~8.9M + molder 2.5M = ~11.4M of demand coverable without the line

slides.so_what: Gates 0–1 risk only $0.6M; Gates 2–3 release $4.2M, only with $3.5M+ committed funding
footnotes: Source: IC briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis
Line producing = 12-month lead time + commissioning, plus up to 2 months of specialty validation; order by Q3 2028 to produce before the 2030 peak
Each gate has a date, a proposed owner and a default: if a trigger is missed, the default is the cheaper, reversible path

lead_message.text: If orders fall short, the plan degrades gracefully: at worst weak demand forfeits the deposit, never breaching the covenant

lead_message.text: We ask the committee for four decisions in January, none of which commits the $4.2M balance

slides.rationale: Four decisions asked of the reader -> numbered list with the cash each commits

items.text: Approve the $0.6M slot deposit for March 2027, on one condition: written terms for an order date of Q1 2028 or later and the lead time; if refused, decline
Decline the full order and any public capacity announcement now; Sales uses the slot and molder plan privately to turn forecasts into signed minimums or prepayments
Authorize the 2028 overflow plan: molder for 0.6M units (about $0.07M of premium), signed by June 2027 with holiday capacity; capped safety stock; validation quote
Adopt the three release triggers and the gate calendar: 10.5M+ units signed or a simulated breach; $3.5M+ committed funding; readiness. Target Q1 2028, last Q3 2028

slides.so_what: Cash committed by these decisions: $0.6M, leaving $8.2M against the $7.0M floor

units.text: Reserve the slot as a capped $0.6M option, bridge 2028 with the contract molder, and order the line only once signed demand and funding clear set triggers
Starting hypothesis (Ops Director: reserve now, gate the order) survives the tests, but only with a funding plan and a flexible order date; H1, H2, H4 hold, H3 partly, H5 not yet, H6 unverified
The gap is real and starts in 2028, but its size hinges on unsigned demand
On accepted units the line is 92% utilized in 2027 (not 83%); overflow from 2028 (0.6M); the '17% free capacity' view divides by nameplate; real slack 0.7M (7.8%)
Specialty runs scrap 4% more and the forecast has no allowance: ~0.09–0.10M units of capacity a year from 2029
Plant has no real buffer for 2028 peaks: the bridge must be in place before the 2028 peak
At forecast overflow reaches 3.5M by 2030; at signed minimums 0.9M; 2.6M (21%) of 2030 volume unsigned; a one-year slip moves the ceiling breach to 2031
Only the forecast case needs a second line before 2031; signed volume should trigger the order

98% fill rate is monthly; two misses allow a rebid of the whole allocation; 2029 demand at 98% of max monthly supply with the molder maxed out (~2% headroom); launch clustering; molder holiday capacity uncommitted; ~$4.0M a year of base contribution exposed
Ordering now leaves $4.0M of cash, $3.0M below the $7.0M floor; no borrowing facility; needs at least $3.0M of new funding; ruled out on cash
The Sales VP's '23% faster growth' claim is cross-sectional and cannot show that building capacity caused growth

Only reserve slot + molder bridge passes every hard constraint while keeping 2030 capacity; order now fails covenant; molder only cheapest to 2029 but 1.0M short in 2030; do nothing fails in the first peak
Recommended path costs ~$5.8M to 2030 (deposit credited), $0.6M less than ordering now ($6.45M) because fixed costs start ~18 months later
The molder is a cheap bridge through 2029 ($0.07–0.27M a year) but at forecast runs out in 2030 (1.0M short, $0.45M lost) and cannot make the specialty product; still keeps $0.33 of $0.45 per unit
The line is insurance for allocations, not a margin play: beats the molder on running cost only above 4.6M overflow units a year; only ~$0.20M a year better in 2030
Slot is a capped option: at most $0.6M at risk, cash $1.2M above the floor; deposit uses a third of the $1.8M headroom; balance still needs $3.0M new money
On lost units alone the deposit is not worth paying (133%); with a rebid it breaks even at 41% / 24% probability, plausible but only if the slot buys timing (H6)
Pay the deposit as insurance only if its order date can be deferred (Q1 2028 or later); otherwise decline
Five conditions make the slot a bad option; the first two (order-by-June date, lead time available without a slot) can be tested before the March deposit
If the supplier will not move the order date, decline the slot and plan on the molder plus a 2028 order at standard lead time, once confirmed
Cover 2028 in three layers: molder (0.6M, $0.07M, signed by 30 June 2027), 2027 safety stock (0.7M slack), specialty in-house with scrap allowance and monthly simulation; total cover 3.2M (~5x)
Only a January 2027 order (which breaches the covenant) gets the line in before the 2028 peak
Demand trigger: signed 2029 or 2030 minimums of 10.5M units or more (today 9.4M / 9.8M), or a simulated fill-rate breach in 2+ months
Funding trigger: at least $3.5M committed, so cash after the $4.2M payment is $7.5M or more (floor + $0.5M buffer)
Readiness trigger: supplier confirms 12-month installation at a fixed price; specialty validation plan (+2 months); molder through commissioning; inflation re-quoted
Not triggers: 'demand is growing', nonbinding forecasts, peer growth statistics, a wish to announce capacity publicly; one contract can meet two triggers
Four decision gates with dates, owners and defaults: Gate 0 Jan 2027 IC, 0b Feb–Mar 2027, Gate 1 by Jun 2027, Gate 2 Q1 2028 target, Gate 3 Q3 2028 last date
Provisional (Gates 0–1): $0.6M at risk, cash ≥ $8.2M; full investment (Gates 2–3): $4.2M only with ≥ $3.5M committed funding
Downside cases: weak demand costs at most the $0.6M deposit, the cash floor holds in every case (lowest $7.5M–$8.0M); demand without funding is a retention risk, mitigated by customer co-funding
Most sensitive to unsigned-demand timing, funding and slot terms (in that order), then monthly peaks, specialty, construction inflation / cash flow; no single one overturns the recommendation
Four decisions in January, none commits the $4.2M: approve conditional deposit; decline full order and public announcement; authorize 2028 overflow plan; adopt triggers and gate calendar
Let Sales use the reserved slot and molder plan privately to turn nonbinding forecasts into signed minimums or prepayments
Next steps with proposed owners and dates: supplier terms, molder RFQ, simulation, funding term sheet, signed-volume talks, 13-week cash forecast
Cash tests exclude 2027–30 operating cash flow (not in pack)
Rebid loss shares 25% / 50% are illustrative
Judgment calls where the pack was silent (slot terms, specialty share, peak timing, trigger and buffer, downside cases) are flagged for the committee
Calculation appendix tracing every figure to pack inputs
